learning_goal: Name the four cuff muscles, say which tubercle each one reaches, and predict the movement lost when one of them tears.

structures.name: right scapula
structures.label: Scapula
structures.narration: All four cuff muscles start on the scapula. Three on the back of it, one on the front.

structures.name: right humerus
structures.label: Humerus
structures.narration: All four end on the top of the humerus, so together they hold its head in the shallow glenoid.

structures.name: right supraspinatus
structures.label: Supraspinatus
structures.narration: Above the spine of the scapula, running under the acromion to the greater tubercle. It starts abduction — the first fifteen degrees — before deltoid takes over.

structures.name: right infraspinatus muscle
structures.label: Infraspinatus
structures.narration: Below the spine, filling the infraspinous fossa. It rotates the arm laterally.

structures.name: right teres minor
structures.label: Teres minor
structures.narration: A narrow strip along the lateral border of the scapula, just below infraspinatus. It also rotates laterally, and it is the one cuff muscle supplied by the axillary nerve.

structures.name: right subscapularis
structures.label: Subscapularis
structures.narration: The only one on the front of the scapula, between the scapula and the ribs. It rotates the arm medially — the opposite of the other three.

structures.name: right teres major
structures.label: Teres major — NOT cuff
structures.narration: Teres major sits right below teres minor and is a favourite exam trap. It is not part of the cuff — it crosses to the front of the humerus and does not blend with the capsule.

structures.name: acromial part of right deltoid
structures.label: Deltoid — acromial part
structures.narration: Deltoid covers the cuff from outside. It takes abduction on after the first fifteen degrees.

structures.name: spinal part of right deltoid
structures.label: Deltoid — spinal part
structures.narration: The back of deltoid, arising from the spine of the scapula — hiding infraspinatus and teres minor beneath it.

structures.label: Greater tubercle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: the most lateral point of the proximal 12% of the humerus, measured on the mesh (14.1 mm lateral of the shaft axis) — see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: Three facets on one bump. Supraspinatus takes the top, infraspinatus the middle, teres minor the lowest.

structures.label: Greater tubercle — superior facet
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and supraspinatus, measured on the source meshes (gap 0.34 mm) — tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA23130 --contact FMA32544
structures.narration: The top facet. Supraspinatus lands here, the highest of the three, which is why its tendon is the one that rubs under the acromion.

structures.label: Greater tubercle — middle facet
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and infraspinatus, measured on the source meshes (gap 0.06 mm) — tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA23130 --contact FMA32547
structures.narration: The middle facet, behind and below the superior one. Infraspinatus lands here.

structures.label: Greater tubercle — inferior facet
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and teres minor, measured on the source meshes (gap 0.23 mm) — tools/derive-landmark.mjs --parent FMA23130 --contact FMA32553
structures.narration: The lowest facet. Teres minor lands here. Measured on the mesh the three sit in the order the textbook gives them — supraspinatus highest, then infraspinatus, then teres minor.

structures.label: Lesser tubercle
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: nearest CONTACT point between the humerus and subscapularis, measured on the source meshes (gap 0.09 mm) — see tools/derive-humerus-landmarks.mjs
structures.narration: The smaller bump in front. Subscapularis alone reaches it — which is why it is the odd one out on movement too.

views.title: See it in the body
views.narration: From behind, deltoid covers everything. The cuff is the layer underneath, wrapped round the shoulder joint.

views.title: Take the deltoid off
views.narration: Now the three posterior cuff muscles show: supraspinatus above the spine, infraspinatus below it, teres minor along the lateral border.

views.title: The fourth one is in front
views.narration: Subscapularis lines the front of the scapula. You never see it from behind, and that is half the reason students forget it.

views.title: Where each one lands
views.narration: Three go to the greater tubercle — supraspinatus to the superior facet, infraspinatus to the middle, teres minor to the inferior — and one, subscapularis, to the lesser. That single fact carries the whole movement story.

views.title: Rotate in, rotate out
views.narration: Subscapularis pulls the front of the humerus medially. Infraspinatus pulls the back of it laterally. Same joint, opposite directions, because they attach on opposite sides.

views.title: Follow supraspinatus
views.narration: It runs from the supraspinous fossa, under the acromion, to the greater tubercle. That tunnel is narrow — squeeze the tendon there and you get the painful arc between sixty and one hundred and twenty degrees.

views.title: The trap: teres major
views.narration: Teres minor is cuff, teres major is not. Minor goes to the greater tubercle and rotates laterally. Major crosses to the front of the humerus and rotates medially.

gaps: RESOLVED 2026-08-29 audit. The catalog has no separate meshes for the three facets of the greater tubercle, but it does not need them: each facet is defined by the tendon that lands on it, and all four cuff meshes are held locally, so each facet was MEASURED as the contact point between the humerus and its muscle — supraspinatus 0.34 mm, infraspinatus 0.06 mm, teres minor 0.23 mm. The three now exist as separate anchors and beat 4 points each muscle at its own facet instead of all three at one bump. The measurement checks itself: the three come out in descending height on the bone (w = 0.982, 0.952, 0.925) in exactly the order the textbook gives them, which is not something a guess would produce.
There is no mesh for the joint capsule or the subacromial bursa, so the cuff's blending with the capsule and the site of subacromial impingement are described but not shown.

CORRECTED 2026-08-29 audit. This note previously said the greater tubercle anchor had to be an EXTREME because no supraspinatus mesh was held locally to measure a contact against. That was false — FMA32544 is in meshes-lite, as are all four cuff muscles, and re-running the contact derivation gave uvw [0.5516, 0.4058, 0.9823] at a gap of 0.34 mm. The greater_tubercle anchor is deliberately LEFT as the extreme, because the extreme is the tubercle as a whole while a contact is one facet of it; the contact measurements are authored as the three new facet anchors instead. The two agree to within 0.06 of a uvw unit, which is the corroboration the extreme never had. The lesser tubercle anchor IS a contact (subscapularis, gap 0.09 mm) and re-derived to the same coordinate this run. All anchors stay status:"needs-review" until a human has looked at them once.
